KEY MESSAGE 1...Daily chances for showers and thunderstorms 
into the middle of the week. There is a risk for strong to 
severe thunderstorms, as well as a marginal risk for localized 
heavy rainfall leading to flash flooding.

A surface cold front will gradually sag southward across the northern
tier of the region this afternoon into evening before stalling around
the I-80 or I-78 corridors come Wednesday. During this time, a few
upper level shortwave pulses will rendezvous with the surface cold
front, bringing rounds of showers and storms through Wednesday morning.
The first round of storms this afternoon and evening will be probably
to the North/West across the southern Poconos and possibly into the
Lehigh Valley. Other more scattered activity is possible across
southern NJ. The upper vort maxs are difficult to track and the
CAMs guidance is very inconsistent, so we'll continue with
blended guidance as well as satellite/radar trends for our
updates. That said, instability across the region does look to
be limited to the 1000-2000 J/kg range with limited deep layer 
shear, which will, therefore, limit the severe weather potential
today. SPC has expanded the Marginal Risk (level 1 out of 5) 
farther northeast now into the Lehigh Valley and central NJ, and
the entire area remains in the Marginal Risk (level 1 out of 4)
for excessive rainfall.

The latest guidance now suggests a second round of showers and 
perhaps some convective thunderstorms to arrive early Wednesday 
morning with the potential for heavy downpours during the 
Wednesday morning rush hour. While there remains a fair amount
of uncertainty with this setup it appears that this round may 
be a result of a decaying upstream MCS from the Ohio Valley. 
This setup remains highly uncertain and fully dependent on how 
the volatile setup across the Ohio Valley eventually pans out 
through the overnight hours. Areas that are favored for higher
pops and heavy rains will be Delmarva and south NJ, possibly
into Philadelphia. 


Additional rounds of upper level shortwaves look to ride along the
quasi-stationary boundary which will support rounds of convection
continuing at least through Wednesday night, and possibly into 
Thursday. The front looks to push through by late Thursday, and 
a much drier and cooler airmass will arrive by Friday and 
Saturday as a result. This will bring us a more pronounced break
in convective potential and more pleasant weather conditions.

KEY MESSAGE 2...Hot and humid conditions will persist into the 
middle of the week, but humidity will not be as oppressive as 
recent days.

A relatively stagnant synoptic pattern will remain in place 
across our region. Quasi zonal mid and upper level flow will be 
in place through the middle of the week as Bermuda high pressure
persists offshore. This will keep a very warm and moist airmass
in place across the region through the period.

Hot and humid conditions will continue into the middle of the
week, although slightly lower temperatures and dewpoints will
arrive for Wednesday. Dewpoints are anticipated to mix out into
the mid to upper 60s again this afternoon. This will give some 
slight reprieve from the excessive humidity we've experienced in
recent days, though highs will still be in the upper 80s to mid
90s. The lower dewpoints will result in maximum heat indices 
mainly in the mid to upper 90s, though could get near 100 
degrees in Delmarva and near the coast in New Jersey. Therefore,
hot and humid, but not to the point where any heat headlines are
needed.

By Friday and Saturday with the front finally having pushed through,
a much drier and more cooler airmass will arrive, which will bring
much more pleasant weather conditions. Dewpoints may drop into the
50s again for many areas with highs forecast to be in the low to
mid 80s. Dewpoints look to start rebounding into the 60s again 
by Sunday.


KEY MESSAGE 3...There is potential for minor tidal flooding 
during the evening high tides this week along the Atlantic 
coast, Delaware Bay, and tidal Delaware River, especially on 
Tuesday and Wednesday.

As we approach the New Moon on Wednesday, astronomical tides for
the evening high tide cycles will increase to around a half foot
below minor flood stage in many areas this week along the 
Atlantic coasts of New Jersey and Delware, Delaware Bay, and 
the tidal Delaware River. With tide departures running around a 
half foot above average, this will raise a threat of minor flood
stage being reached for these areas.

We will continue to monitor the tide departures in the coming
total water level forecasts. Coastal Flood Advisories have been
issued for areas along the Delaware Bay for the Tuesday evening
high tide. Additional Coastal Flood Advisories may be needed 
over the coming days, but at least spotty minor tidal flooding 
should be anticipated around the times of the evening high tides
